correctness.rationale: For p>8 the five quadratic polynomials have exactly nine distinct branch roots, with the sole duplicated root shared by j=0 and j=4. Expanding the 32-normalized sign indicator and applying Weil to squarefree subsets gives coefficient 129, reduced to 113 over eight double-root subsets, with correction 8+144=152. Hence 32N>=p-113sqrt(p)-152, positive above 14000. The exact standard-library checker enumerates all 1651 odd primes below 14000 and all patterns; independent Euler-criterion checks cover the first 250 primes; at 233 only mask zero is absent. No probabilistic inference or incomplete search is used.

value.rationale: A canonical natural invariant of SL2(F_p) is split vs nonsplit regular semisimple type as a function of trace discriminant. Five consecutive traces are the first window with shared branch roots, so the simultaneous 32-word realization cutoff is structurally motivated rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The theorem gives an exact best threshold and complete exceptional primes, with the one-word obstruction at the sharp boundary.
